        Page drafted with an AI coding assistant; see the disclosure in the guide.

        Knowledge Graphs playground

        Write RDF, check it with SHACL and ask it questions with SPARQL. Everything runs in this page; nothing is sent to a server.

        Create KG

        Write a recipe in Turtle and see it drawn as a graph.

        Validate KG

        Check a graph against SHACL shapes and see which rules it breaks.

        Query KG

        Ask the recipe graph questions in SPARQL, starting from the worksheet queries.

        The engine: rete

        rete (Latin for “net”) stores a whole RDF graph in one immutable .rete file: the term dictionary, the sorted triple indexes and a dataset card. Put the file on any static host and clients run SPARQL against it where it sits, the idea of Parquet or PMTiles applied to RDF graphs.

        This page embeds the rete engine, version , compiled to WebAssembly, together with the recipe graph of the course (). rete is experimental: the file format can change before version 1.0, so a .rete file must be read by the version that wrote it.

        github.com/caviri/rete · guide and exercises · course repository

        Guide

        Exercises for the hands-on parts of the course.

        What it is

        rete stores a whole RDF graph in one immutable .rete file: the terms, the sorted triple indexes and a dataset card. This page embeds the rete engine (WebAssembly) and recipes.rete, the course graph of 807 triples in 48 KB. It is one HTML file: save it and it works from disk, offline. It supports the hands-on parts of the course: writing your own data (H1), validating it with SHACL (H2) and querying (H3).

        Exercises

        1 · Query the recipe graph 10 min

        1. Go to Query KG and pick q04 in the sidebar. Predict the answer, then press Run (or Ctrl+Enter) to read it.
        2. Change PT30M to PT45M. The old answer is dimmed until you run the query again.
        3. Delete the last } and run it. The status line says where the query stops being valid, the line is marked in the margin, and the last good answer stays on screen, dimmed.
        4. Open q09, add a third diet or remove one, and run it. Switch the answer to Cards.

        2 · Put an answer on a map 5 min

        1. Open q20 and run it: where do the ingredients grow? The lab draws a map when a query returns ?lat and ?long (or a WKT POINT).
        2. A numeric variable sets the size of each point, another one its label. Change the query to count recipes per country instead of foods.

        3 · Write your own recipe 15 min

        1. Switch to Create KG in the top bar. A starter recipe is there; the status line tells you whether it is valid, and the right pane draws the graph as you type. By class shows it as one table per class, Triples as a plain list.
        2. Replace it with a recipe of your own. Reuse the food:, cuisine: and course: IRIs of the course; Turtle example in the sidebar brings the starter back.
        3. Open Dataset card… and say what your graph is: title, description, licence, creators. Add as many creators, organizations and example queries as you need; keywords are added with Enter. The right side shows the card as a reader will see it. YAML holds the same card as text, and the two stay in step. The engine checks the fields, and the card is stored in the .rete file.
        4. Set Combine with to Recipes. Your triples and the course graph become one .rete file, held in memory.
        5. Press Query this graph (it takes you to Query KG) and run q01, q04 and q09 again. Does your recipe show up where you expect it?
        6. Write a query of your own and press + Add as example. It is listed under “Your examples” and written into the card of your graph.
        7. Back in Create KG, the download buttons save the graph as a .rete file, as Turtle or as JSON-LD. Send the .rete to your neighbour, who opens it in Query KG with Open file… and reads its card. Every graph in the Query KG sidebar has the same three downloads.

        4 · Validate a graph 10 min

        1. Switch to Validate KG. The SHACL shapes of the course are in the editor. Press Validate: the recipe graph conforms to them.
        2. Open Broken data to try, pick b01 and press Validate. The shape it breaks is highlighted in the editor, with the cursor on it. Which node breaks it, and what does the message ask for? Try b08 and b11; click a row of the report to jump to its shape.
        3. Change a shape, for example raise sh:minCount of the ingredients to 3, choose Recipes under Graph to validate and validate again.
        4. Choose the graph you created under Graph to validate and validate it. Does your recipe conform? Repair it in Create KG until it does.
        This page validates SHACL Core with the rete engine. rete 0.7.8 does not report sh:not applied to the values of a path, which the diet rules of the course shapes use: a vegan recipe with butter (b05) passes here. That file is left out of the list; use the validator of the H2 worksheet for those rules.

        5 · Open a graph from the web 5 min

        1. In Query KG, paste https://caviri.github.io/rete/docs/plaza/data/linked-jazz.rete under Add a graph and press Open.
        2. You know nothing about this graph. Find its predicates first: 
          SELECT ?p (COUNT(*) AS ?n) WHERE { ?s ?p ?o } GROUP BY ?p ORDER BY DESC(?n)
        3. Copy link gives a URL that reopens the same graph, query and view.
        A host must send CORS headers for the lab to read a .rete file from it. GitHub Pages does. The lab downloads the whole file, so keep to files of a few megabytes.

        Around the page

        • All options (top right) shows the tools you rarely need: other graphs, downloads, the dataset card, CSV and links.
        • ☰ in the top bar hides and shows the sidebar.
        • Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac) in the editor does the same as Run or Validate.
        • Drag the line between the editor and the results to give one of them more room; double-click it to reset. With the keyboard: focus it and use the arrow keys.
        • A table wider than its pane has a scrollbar above and below it.

        Links that open a query

        Worksheets and slides can link straight into this page. The query is loaded, not run: the reader presses Run. The part after # takes:

        ParameterMeaning
        qthe SPARQL query, URL-encoded
        urla .rete file to open and query instead of the built-in graph
        viewtable (default), cards or map
        tabwelcome, create, validate, query or guide; a link with q or url opens Query KG
        index.html#view=cards&q=SELECT%20%3Fs%20WHERE%20%7B%20%3Fs%20a%20%3Chttps%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FRecipe%3E%20%7D

        Rebuild

        From a checkout of sdsc-ordes/rdf-training, after just setup:

        bash src/rete/build-rete.sh   # docs/data/recipes.rete, then docs/index.html (or: just rete)
node src/rete/check-lab.mjs   # drive the page in a browser                  (or: just check-rete)
        • build-rete.sh concatenates the ontology, the SKOS value lists and the instance data from src/data/ and runs rete build. It uses the rete command-line tool at the version pinned in the script and downloads the release binary, checked against its SHA-256 sum, when that version is not installed.
        • build-lab.mjs inlines the engine (rete-graph from npm, same version), the .rete file, the worksheet queries, the course shapes, the broken files of the H2 worksheet and a world outline into the template src/rete/lab.html and writes docs/index.html, this page.
        • The file format is not stable before rete 1.0: the command-line tool and the engine in the page must be the same version. Rebuild after changing the data, the queries or either version.

        AI disclosure

        This page, its build and check scripts and the map query q20 were written with an AI coding assistant: Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2, Anthropic) running in Claude Code, directed by a course maintainer.

        • Strategy. Two sub-agents worked in parallel before any code was written: one read the rete repository (file format, command-line tool, JavaScript API, hosting rules), the other mapped this repository (site, hands-on files, tests, build). The main agent then wrote the code and the text from their reports.
        • Checks. The claims above were tested, not assumed: the Python test suite, the JavaScript cross-check, and check-lab.mjs, which runs every worksheet query in the built page and compares the row counts with the course snapshots, and validates the broken files of the H2 worksheet against their expected results. The screenshots in the repository (docs/img/) are written by that script.
        • Human part. The requirements, the layout of the page and the choice to keep the map coordinates in the course data came from the maintainer. The course data, ontology and worksheet queries q01 to q19 are not AI-generated by this change.
        • Not AI. Nothing in this page calls a language model. Queries run in the rete engine inside the page.
